preamble: The diphthong [oi] becomes [ai] when its mid back rounded nucleus unrounds and lowers to [a]. The best-known cases are not independent diphthong changes but side effects of a branch-wide merger of PIE *o with *a: in Proto-Germanic, PIE *oy became *ai (PIE *h₁óynos 'one' > Proto-Germanic *ainaz > Gothic ains), and the same merger in Balto-Slavic turned *oy into *ai (Proto-Balto-Slavic *aiˀnas 'one', Old Prussian ains).

examples.note: Part of the Proto-Germanic merger of PIE *o and *a; the diphthong *oy fell together with *ay.
The o-grade perfect diphthong surfaces as *ai in the Germanic preterite-present verb *witaną.
Balto-Slavic also merged PIE *o with *a, so *oy became *ai; Lithuanian vienas continues the same form with a prothetic v- and later ai > ie.

sources: Kroonen, G. (2013). Etymological Dictionary of Proto-Germanic. Brill. https://brill.com/display/title/20925
Wikipedia (2026). Proto-Germanic language: Merging of non-high back vowels. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proto-Germanic_language
